newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia wants extradition of suspected paedophile.
newsitem.headline: Australia wants extradition of suspected paedophile.

text.p: Australia has sent a police officer from its child protection task force to South Africa to make a formal plea for the extradition of suspected Australian paedophile Phillip Bell.
Police Minister for the state government of New South Wales Paul Whelan said on Saturday Bell would face a South African court for an extradition hearing there on Monday.
Bell, 62, was arrested in South Africa on Friday in connection with about 200 charges of child sexual abuse. He was remanded in custody following a brief court appearance on Friday.
Bell had been on the run from Interpol and had apparently tried to settle in the popular Eastern Cape surfing resort of Jeffreys Bay.
"He has to appear before a South African court and a South African judge of that court to determine whether extradition should be granted," Whelan told Australian Associated Press.

Whelan said the police officer sent to South Africa was attached to a task force set up to investigate child sexual abuse allegations arising from a royal commission of inquiry into police corruption in New South Wales.
